Declare the Huff model

Source: R/06-ae_workflow.R
huff_allocation.Rd

Declare the Huff model, a conditional logit allocation without an outside option, on prepared allocation inputs.

Usage

huff_allocation(
  inputs,
  family = "power",
  kappa = 1,
  beta = 1,
  fit_beta = TRUE,
  by_group = character(),
  fixed = NULL
)

Arguments

inputs

An ae_prepared_inputs object from checked preparation.

family

Travel kernel, as in clm_allocation(): "power" (the default, Huff's form), "gaussian", "exponential", a declaration from decay_kernel(), or for inputs with demand groups a named list with one of these per group.

kappa

Positive supply scale used in attractiveness, not in reported raw supply or capacity attribution.

beta

Positive exponent on attractiveness in (kappa * supply)^beta: the value held fixed when fit_beta = FALSE.

fit_beta

TRUE (the default) fits beta as a parameter; FALSE holds it at the given value.

by_group

For inputs with demand groups: "sigma" lets the decay differ by group (default none). "v0" is refused, since the Huff model has no outside option.

fixed

For inputs with demand groups: a named numeric vector of parameters held fixed, as in clm_allocation(). Names of outside weights (v0) are refused.

Value

The model: an ae_problem for the static CLM with no outside option. Parameter order is sigma, then beta when it is fitted. With demand groups sigma is sigma.<group> for the groups in by_group.

Details

The Huff model (Huff, 1963) gives each facility a share of each origin's demand in proportion to its attractiveness times a decay in travel time: P_ij = a_j W(d_ij) / sum_k a_k W(d_ik), where a_j = (kappa * S_j)^beta for facility supply S_j. Every origin's demand is shared among the facilities, so the shares at an origin add up to 1.

This is the conditional logit model of clm_allocation() without an outside option: huff_allocation() calls clm_allocation() with v0 = 0 and returns the same kind of model, so fit_allocation(), evaluate_allocation(), predict_allocation(), check_allocation() and compare_allocations() work on it unchanged. Use clm_allocation(fit_v0 = TRUE) when part of the demand goes to facilities that are not in the data.

With the default power decay, W(d) = d^(-sigma), so spax's sigma is Huff's distance exponent and beta is his exponent on attractiveness. Both are fitted by default (fit_beta = TRUE); with beta = 1 and fit_beta = FALSE, attractiveness is proportional to supply. Power decay is undefined at a travel time of 0, so use a positive minimum travel time or another kernel (family).

The facility bootstrap bootstrap_allocation() needs a fitted outside weight and so does not apply to a Huff model.

References

Huff DL (1963). A probabilistic analysis of shopping center trade areas. Land Economics 39(1):81-90. doi:10.2307/3144521

See also

clm_allocation() for the general model with an outside option.

Other allocation steps: bootstrap_fit(), calc_demand(), calc_travel_time(), check_fit(), clm_allocation(), compare_fits(), decay_kernel(), evaluate_allocation(), fit_allocation(), predict_allocation(), prepare_allocation()

Examples

# Mainland Cornwall: small areas share their registered residents among the
# practices in proportion to attractiveness times travel-time decay.
areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa[!cornwall_lsoa$scilly, ])
gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp[!cornwall_gp$scilly, ])
travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice]

# Without an outside option, demand is the residents registered at the
# mainland practices
demand <- stats::setNames(areas$registered_in, areas$lsoa)
supply <- stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice)
inputs <- prepare_allocation(demand, supply, travel)

# Power decay with a fitted attractiveness exponent
model <- huff_allocation(inputs)

# Evaluate at given parameters: distance exponent 2, attractiveness
# exponent 1
evaluate_allocation(model, c(sigma = 2, beta = 1))
#> <allocation evaluation>
#> converged: TRUE
#> iterations: 1
#> error: 0
#> residual_norm: 0

# Fit practice totals of registrations from two starts
totals <- tapply(cornwall_flows$patients, cornwall_flows$practice, sum)
observed <- stats::setNames(numeric(ncol(travel)), colnames(travel))
observed[intersect(names(totals), names(observed))] <-
  totals[intersect(names(totals), names(observed))]
fit <- fit_allocation(
  model, observed,
  starts = rbind(a = c(sigma = 1, beta = 0.5), b = c(sigma = 3, beta = 1.5)),
  lower = c(sigma = 0.1, beta = 0.05), upper = c(sigma = 10, beta = 5),
  loss = "poisson"
)
fit$best$theta
#>     sigma      beta 
#> 1.0415962 0.6062301
